# windows_net_route (Resource)

Manages one persistent IP route on one network interface of a remote Windows host (`New-NetRoute` / `Set-NetRoute` / `Remove-NetRoute -PolicyStore PersistentStore` via SSH and PowerShell): static routes to remote networks, on-link routes, and manually managed default gateways.

`interface_alias`, `destination_prefix` and `next_hop` identify the route and are immutable after creation (ForceNew); only `route_metric` is updated in place. `destination_prefix` must be in canonical masked CIDR form (`10.0.0.5/24` is a plan-time error that names `10.0.0.0/24`); `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` are default routes. `next_hop` must be the same family as the prefix; `0.0.0.0` / `::` means on-link (no gateway).

Route metric vs interface metric: Windows selects routes by longest prefix first, then by the lowest **effective metric** (`route_metric` + `interface_metric`). This resource manages the route metric; the interface metric is observed. Adding a manual default route with a **higher** effective metric than the existing one is the supported "backup gateway" pattern: the existing route keeps winning until it disappears.

Safety — this resource changes routing for the whole host and can sever its own SSH session: deleting, replacing or re-metricing the route that carries the provider's own SSH return traffic is refused fail-closed, as is creating or updating a route that would hijack that traffic. When the management path cannot be determined the operation is refused as well. `unsafe_skip_management_check` bypasses the guard entirely: the change may apply and still end in an apply error (transport lost, timeout), and the host must stay reachable at the provider `host` address afterwards. Consider a `precondition` on the `windows_net_route` data source reading back the default route before changing gateways.

Import format: `<interface_alias>|<destination_prefix>|<next_hop>`. Only routes with protocol `NetMgmt` are importable; automatic routes (`Local` on-link routes derived from addresses, `Dhcp` gateways) are refused with a clear error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Static route to a remote network (storage network) through a gateway on
# the same subnet. The gateway must be on-link on the interface; on-link
# routes below use the unspecified address instead.
resource "windows_net_route" "backup" {
  destination_prefix = "198.51.100.0/24" # documentation range, RFC 5737
  interface_alias    = "Ethernet 2"
  next_hop           = "192.0.2.1"
  route_metric       = 10

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly. Without this block each operation
  # defaults to 10 minutes; a stalled PowerShell/SSH session then surfaces a
  # timeout diagnostic instead of blocking Terraform indefinitely.
  timeouts = {
    create = "10m"
    read   = "5m"
    update = "10m"
    delete = "10m"
  }
}

# On-link route (no gateway): the next hop is the unspecified address.
resource "windows_net_route" "onlink" {
  destination_prefix = "203.0.113.0/24" # documentation range, RFC 5737
  interface_alias    = "Ethernet 2"
  next_hop           = "0.0.0.0"
}

# Backup default gateway: a higher effective metric than the existing default
# route means this route stays idle until that route disappears. Only
# route_metric updates in place; changing the prefix, next hop or interface
# replaces the resource.
resource "windows_net_route" "backup_gateway" {
  destination_prefix = "0.0.0.0/0"
  interface_alias    = "Ethernet 2"
  next_hop           = "192.0.2.254"
  route_metric       = 500
}

# Guard a default-gateway change with a precondition on the current default
# route: refuse to apply when the live gateway is not the expected one.
resource "windows_net_route" "default" {
  destination_prefix = "0.0.0.0/0"
  interface_alias    = "Ethernet 2"
  next_hop           = "192.0.2.1"
  route_metric       = 256

  lifecycle {
    precondition {
      condition     = data.windows_net_route.current_default.next_hop == "192.0.2.1"
      error_message = "The live default gateway changed out-of-band; re-check before replacing it."
    }
  }
}

output "backup_effective_metric" {
  value       = windows_net_route.backup.effective_metric
  description = "Effective metric (route + interface) Windows uses to select the backup route."
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `destination_prefix` (String) Route destination in CIDR form (e.g. `"198.51.100.0/24"`, `"0.0.0.0/0"` for the IPv4 default route). Must be in canonical masked form: host bits set is a plan-time error that names the canonical form. Immutable after creation (ForceNew).
- `interface_alias` (String) Network interface alias (e.g. `"Ethernet 2"`). Matched exactly and case-insensitively, never as a wildcard. Immutable after creation (ForceNew). Must not contain `|` (used as the import-ID separator).
- `next_hop` (String) Gateway address in canonical spelling. Must be the same family as `destination_prefix`. `0.0.0.0` / `::` means on-link (no gateway). Multicast and loopback addresses are rejected. Immutable after creation (ForceNew).

### Optional

- `route_metric` (Number) Route metric (0-9999). Added to the interface metric to form the effective metric Windows uses for route selection. Updated in place. Defaults to `256` (the Windows default).
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `unsafe_skip_management_check` (Boolean) Bypasses the management-path guard entirely. The change may apply and still end in an apply error (transport lost, timeout); the host must stay reachable at the provider `host` address afterwards. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `address_family` (String) Address family, as observed on the host: `IPv4` or `IPv6`.
- `effective_metric` (Number) Effective metric Windows uses for route selection (`route_metric` + `interface_metric`), as observed on the host.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier: `<interface_alias>|<destination_prefix>|<next_hop>`.
- `interface_index` (Number) Numeric interface index owning the route, as observed on the host.
- `interface_metric` (Number) Interface metric from `Get-NetIPInterface`, as observed on the host.
- `protocol` (String) Route protocol, as observed on the host: `NetMgmt` for routes this resource creates.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing persistent route by <interface_alias>|<destination_prefix>|<next_hop>.
# Only routes with protocol NetMgmt are importable; automatic routes (Local
# on-link routes derived from addresses, Dhcp gateways) are refused.
terraform import windows_net_route.backup "Ethernet 2|198.51.100.0/24|192.0.2.1"
```
